Subject: Candidate adjudication: Samir Patel — on-site debrief and scorecards

Hi all,

Thanks for taking the time to interview Samir for SWE II earlier today. Quick ask: please fill out the attached scorecard by EOD tomorrow so we can sync on a fast decision. I'm trying to avoid dragging this through a long cycle — the recruiter has follow-ups ready and Samir is considering another offer.

Key fields: overall recommendation (hire / no-hire / on-hold), rubric scores (system design, implementation, collaboration), and 2–3 sentence rationale. If you have a short sample snippet you want captured, paste it into the comments area.

Attachments: scorecard-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Neha — can you aggregate and propose a 30-min consensus slot on Friday? I'll chair and make the call if needed.

Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Candidate adjudication: Samir Patel — on-site debrief and scorecards

Neha/Marissa — filing my quick scorecard now (also added inline here for a fast read):
- System design: 3/5 — asked good clarifying Qs but kept to smaller-scale patterns; missed tradeoff on caching TTLs.
- Implementation: 4/5 — clear, fast whiteboard; example code was idiomatic JS, handled edge cases.
- Collaboration: 5/5 — great thought partnership, asked for constraints and iterated.

Recommendation: hire (strong IC, team fit).

Comment: If we need to be picky, he could use a bit more depth on distributed systems, but for SWE II I think he'd ramp quickly.

--Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Candidate adjudication: Samir Patel — on-site debrief and scorecards

Filing my detailed feedback here — sorry for the delay, had two back-to-back interviews this morning.
- System design: 2/5 — thought process was ok but he struggled to generalize the single-node solution to a sharded design when I pushed on scale >10M qps. Follow-up prompts about consistency tradeoffs didn't land.
- Implementation: 3/5 — clean code but missed a couple of edge cases; would need paired programming early on.
- Collaboration: 4/5 — open to feedback and admitted gaps, good questions about product context.

Recommendation: on-hold for a possible IC hire with mentoring plan OR consider for an engineered IC role that pairs with a stronger systems peer. I lean on-hold.

I added a short note in the aggregate doc about follow-up question areas (caching and cross-region ordering).

-Hannah
Senior Staff Engineer, Reliability
Redwood Inference
